title: Newton's Laws of Motion Module 1 Lesson 2: Resistive Medium custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A small metal sphere of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ falls vertically through oil. The oil exerts a constant upward resistance force of $2\text{ N}$ on the sphere. Calculate the acceleration of the sphere.

A buoyant probe of mass $0.25\text{ kg}$ moves vertically downwards through water. The water exerts a constant upward resistance force of $3.5\text{ N}$ on the probe. Find the deceleration of the probe.

A particle of mass $0.2\text{ kg}$ is projected vertically upwards through a viscous liquid. The liquid exerts a constant downward resistance force of $1.6\text{ N}$ on the particle. Find the deceleration of the particle.

A wooden post of mass $40\text{ kg}$ is driven vertically into the ground. At the instant it strikes the ground, the post moves downwards and experiences a constant resistance force of $2400\text{ N}$ from the soil. Calculate the deceleration of the post.
A diver of mass $70\text{ kg}$ enters the water vertically with a downward deceleration of $6\text{ m s}^{-2}$. Find the magnitude of the upward resistance force exerted by the water on the diver.

A small pellet of mass $0.3\text{ kg}$ is projected vertically upwards through a liquid with initial speed $4.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The liquid exerts a constant resistance force of $1.8\text{ N}$. Find the distance the pellet rises through the liquid before coming to instantaneous rest.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A block of mass $0.6\text{ kg}$ enters a deep tank of fluid moving vertically downwards with speed $5.4\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The fluid exerts a constant upward resistance force of $7.8\text{ N}$ on the block. Show that the deceleration of the block is $3\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the time taken for the block to come to rest, and find the distance it descends through the fluid during this time.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A steel stake of mass $80\text{ kg}$ is driven vertically into the earth. It enters the ground with speed $7.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and penetrates a distance of $0.45\text{ m}$ before stopping. Calculate the deceleration of the stake in the ground.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the magnitude of the constant resistance force exerted by the ground on the stake.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A particle of mass $0.4\text{ kg}$ is projected vertically upwards from the bottom of a pool of depth $2.5\text{ m}$ with initial speed $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The water exerts a constant downward resistance force of $1.6\text{ N}$ on the particle. Calculate the upward deceleration of the particle in the water, and find the speed with which it emerges at the water surface.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: After emerging from the water, the particle rises freely in the air under gravity alone. Find the greatest height reached by the particle above the water surface.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A ball of mass $0.2\text{ kg}$ is dropped from rest from a height of $4.05\text{ m}$ above the surface of a deep lake. Find the speed of the ball immediately before it enters the water.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: On entering the water, the ball experiences a constant upward resistance force of $3.8\text{ N}$. Find the depth to which the ball sinks before coming to instantaneous rest, and calculate the total time elapsed from the moment the ball is dropped until it comes to instantaneous rest in the water.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A stone of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ is projected vertically downwards into a tank of oil with speed $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$. A constant upward resistance force $R$ acts on the stone while in the oil. The stone reaches a depth of $3.2\text{ m}$ in the oil with speed $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the acceleration of the stone in the oil, and hence determine the magnitude of the resistance force $R$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: The stone is subsequently retrieved and projected vertically upwards into the same oil with initial speed $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Assuming the resistance force has the same constant magnitude of $2.5\text{ N}$, find the maximum distance the stone rises through the oil and the time taken to reach this highest point.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A research probe of mass $0.3\text{ kg}$ is fired vertically upwards from the bed of an artificial reservoir with speed $8\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The water has a depth of $1.5\text{ m}$ and exerts a constant downward resistance force of $1.8\text{ N}$ while the probe ascends. Show that the acceleration of the probe in the water is $-16\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and calculate the speed with which it emerges at the water surface.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the maximum height above the water surface reached by the probe, and the time taken from leaving the water to reach this maximum height.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The probe then falls from its highest point back down through the air and re-enters the water. Assuming that the water now exerts a constant upward resistance force of $4.8\text{ N}$ on the descending probe, find the depth to which the probe sinks before coming to rest.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A heavy projectile of mass $0.4\text{ kg}$ is dropped from rest from a height of $7.2\text{ m}$ above a layer of soft ground. Find the speed with which the projectile strikes the ground, and show that if the ground exerts a constant resistance force of $84\text{ N}$, the deceleration of the projectile in the ground is $200\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the depth to which the projectile penetrates the ground before stopping, and calculate the total time elapsed from release until the projectile comes to rest.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The projectile is now dropped from a different height $H\text{ m}$ into another medium which exerts a constant resistance of $R\text{ N}$. Given that the projectile penetrates to a depth of $d\text{ m}$ before stopping, show that $R = mg\left(1 + \frac{H}{d}\right)$, and calculate the resistance force if a drop from $5.4\text{ m}$ results in a penetration depth of $0.20\text{ m}$.
